parameters.content:
## SEO Agent v4 — read me first
**Modes:** I know my keyword · Suggest keywords · Describe my website · Audit my website · Check if my keyword is right · **Rank my site for a keyword** (ladder) · **Track my site** (weekly Search Console / GA4 / Trends report through the Site Tracker workflow; blog posts per week through the Content Cadence workflow) · **I published a page** (publish check + tracking of the live URL) · **Search Console check-in** (monthly: manual action / security issue / Pages report export, the items Google offers no API for) · **Write a case study** (intake → stored proof + case-study page run) · **Check my AI visibility** / **Check my backlinks** (on-demand runs of the AI Visibility Tracker / Backlink Monitor) · **Set up my business profile** (author, reviewer, address: byline, author box, Person / LocalBusiness schema on every page). Same pipeline via the API: the separate workflow **SEO Agent — API** owns `POST /webhook/seo-keyword-check` (header auth; body: `mode`, `keyword`, `country`, `domain`, `business`, `email`, `callback_url`), answers **202 immediately**, and starts this workflow through *API Entry*. Results are POSTed to `callback_url` (or emailed). n8n does not allow Respond-to-Webhook nodes downstream of a Form Trigger, which is why the API lives in its own workflow.

**Credentials to attach before the first run** (none are attached in this copy):
1. DataForSEO — HTTP Basic Auth (22 HTTP nodes)
2. Jina Reader — Header Auth `Authorization: Bearer …` (Read Website, Read Competitor Pages, Read Competitor Homes)
3. Google PageSpeed — Header Auth `X-Goog-Api-Key` (PageSpeed)
4. Gmail SMTP — credential "Gmail SMTP (SEO Agent)": smtp.gmail.com:465, your Gmail address + a Google App Password (Send Report, Send Audit Report)
5. Form basic auth (Start Form) · Webhook header auth (Webhook Trigger)
6. Anthropic API key — credential "Anthropic (SEO Agent)" (all 8 model nodes)
7. PDF rendering needs the `gotenberg` service from compose.override.yml (falls back to .doc if it is down)

**Config** lives at the top of *Normalize Input* (brand, crawl size, QA rounds, countries). Rate limits are in *Rate Limit*.
**Error handling:** set Settings → Error workflow to "SEO Agent — Error Handler" so failed runs page you.
**Testing without spending API credits:** the harness in `n8n/seo-agent/harness/` runs every Code node against fixtures.

### Intake & validation
Forms / webhook → **Normalize Input** (one normalised object: mode, keyword, domain, country codes, deliverables) → **Rate Limit** → **Input OK?**
Validation problems are *data*, not crashes: form users get a "Something needs fixing" page; API requests that fail here are reported to their callback_url. (The API workflow already rejects malformed requests with 400 and acknowledges good ones with 202.)

### Keyword pipeline (keyword / verdict / discover-chained)
Sitemap -> real internal-link candidates + existing-page detection -> **client pages read** (existing page, homepage, one service page: real facts, not placeholders) -> SERP (top 30, PAA, AI Overview, forum threads) -> 6 competitor pages (Jina, 9k chars each) -> **term model** (phrases the top pages share), questions, statistics -> **verified facts** with sources (second search) -> **Competitor Analyzer** (information gain, reader questions, winning formats) -> keyword metrics + **site authority** -> **Verdict** (GO / GO_WITH_CHANGES / AVOID, expected visits, time to rank) -> **Strategy Brief** (Opus, thinking) -> **Copywriter** (Opus, thinking; strict specificity and anti-filler rules) -> **Critic** (Sonnet) -> **Content QA** (content score 0-100: structure, topic coverage, readability, specificity, clean language, length) -> **Editor** (Opus, up to 2 rounds) -> PDF + Word -> download / email / API callback.

### Site audit (technical) — DataForSEO On-Page crawl
Start Crawl (≤200 pages, resources loaded, micromarkup validated) → poll every 60 s (max 25 min) → pages + extra reports (duplicate tags, non-indexable, redirect chains) → **host probes** (apex/www/http, no redirects) + **content probes** (robots, sitemap, llms.txt, 11 crawler user-agents, redirects followed) → **Analyze Probes**.
Technical-only reports go straight to **Build Site Issues**.

### Full SEO Report modules (sequential today — candidates for parallel sub-workflows)
Key-page HTML & schema → competitor discovery (Labs + live SERPs) → domain overview & age → ranked keywords / keyword ideas / gap → backlinks & link gap → PageSpeed (you + competitors) → E-E-A-T content review (Claude) → AI visibility (brand SERP, site: estimate, AI Overviews, live ChatGPT/Perplexity answers).
Every module appends to `extra_findings` / `extra_works`; **Build Site Issues** scores and ranks everything.

### Scoring & reports
Categories start at 100; deductions Critical 30 / High 15 / Medium 7 / Low 3 / Info 1, scaled by share of pages affected, with 70% diminishing returns per severity inside a category. Data-availability notes and AI-written content findings are listed but never scored. Caps: 1 critical → 70, 2+ → 60, 5+ high → 85.
Reports are Word-compatible `.doc` (HTML). Consider real DOCX/PDF for enterprise clients.

### Run ledger (v4.14, D1 — concurrency-safe guards)
Every execution appends one row to **seo_run_ledger** (run_id, key, mode, est_usd, created_at, status, settled_usd) *before* **Rate Limit** counts, so parallel executions no longer overwrite each other's counters (workflow static data did: 8 runs counted as 5). Rate Limit counts the period's rows with a lower id than its own (row order decides ties), skips refused rows and the Keyword Check's rows, and refuses over the same limits as before (6 / day per e-mail, 40 / day per app company, 150 / day in total, `ai_budget_usd` per period). A refused run marks its row (**Mark Run Refused**); every branch settles it at its own end (**Settle Run Ledger**: done, settled_usd) — P1-1: the short modes used to leave the row `reserved` for ever. The settle update matches `status = reserved`, so a row settles once and a refused row stays refused. One insert + one filtered read per run; the table is created on first use.

### One site model (G19, v4.15)
Every workflow reads the same facts about a site through **SM** (`v5/code/_site_model.js`): the **canonical host** (every URL we emit), the business **name / logo / NAP** (profile -> homepage Organization / LocalBusiness schema -> Google Business Profile -> what the app sent), the **services** and nav pages, the **page inventory** (`seo_pages`), the **business facts** and call to action, the brand names, the competitors and the accreditation status. Stored in the `seo_sites` model columns, resolved **weekly** by the Site Tracker and **on demand** here (reused for 7 days, else the homepage is read once; the rebuilt model is cached in `seo_cache` `model:`). See `SITE_MODEL_SPEC.md`.

### Every written page is logged (v4.14, FIX_PLAN D5)
`Blog Package` -> **Content Log Row** -> **Save Content Log (Run)**: one `seo_content_log` row per content run, upserted by `site_id` + `keyword`, status **written**. Ladder page runs were invisible before (only the Content Cadence and the web app wrote rows), so the **pile-up guard** undercounted the pages waiting to be published. The row keeps what the opening row knows (`source`, the week, the last published URL); "I published a page" and the Site Tracker's publish detection set `published`.

### A page someone can publish (FIX_PLAN D10)
The business **name / logo / NAP** come from the **site model** (profile -> homepage `Organization` / `LocalBusiness` schema -> Google Business Profile), not from the business profile alone, and the merged profile travels on to the package's NAP block and author box. A **cost or timeline angle** needs price or timeline facts (`SM.facts`): without them *Parse Brief* drops that angle, its information gain and the table column. *Parse Brief* **clamps the length** to the verdict's own target ("about 2,100 words"), else to the competitor analysis' recommendation, +/-10%, and scales the outline with it. **Content QA fails** a draft with more than **5 placeholders** (notes with a colon do not count) or more than **25% over target**. The **page type** is one of the form's fixed options (`v5/code/_page_type.js`); the verdict's sentence travels as `page_notes`.

### The pages the site already has (D11, v4.15)
The Site Tracker writes a **page inventory** per website into `seo_pages` every Monday (the sitemap, the Search Console pages with the queries they get impressions for, AI Growth's key pages, the pages found live) and *Load Pages (Model)* brings it into this run's site model. **Ladder Plan**, **discovery**, the **Rank Tracker**, the **Site Tracker** and the **Content Cadence** all ask `SM.matchPage(model, keyword)` first: a page answers a search when 75% of the keyword's meaningful words are in its slug or title, or when it already gets impressions for that exact query. A hit means *refresh that page* — never a second page for the same search.

### What the numbers are allowed to say (D20 / D21 / G9 / G24 / G28, v4.15)
**Discovery** loads the site's own **keyword ladders** (*Load Domain Ladders (Discovery)*): a keyword a ladder head or rung already covers is marked `ladder_covered` and is never the next thing to write — one search, one page. An **AI Overview** is claimed only from the *live* check, with the date it was seen; the undated stored value is labelled *historical*. Top domains are deduplicated before the first five, and callback CPCs are rounded to 2 decimals.
**Audit:** *GSC Audit Findings* reports **crawl coverage** — crawled X of Y known URLs (sitemap ∪ the Search Console pages) — and flags under 90%, so nobody reads a finding's share as a share of the whole site.
**Site Tracker** (built in `build_site_tracker.py`): every Search Console row is read (25,000 per request + further pages), the withheld queries are reported as the **anonymised share**, **brand / non-brand** is split with the known brand names, scraper queries are counted apart with the audit's own rule (`_gsc_queries.js`), a **sparse** Trends series carries no percentage, and a traffic alert needs a **statistically real** change (`_site_stats.js`, two-sample Poisson z, 95%) — a big move at low volume is a "Watch", not a fall.

**CrUX Targets → Fetch CrUX → Analyze CrUX** (between the entity check and the scoring, both audit types): the Chrome UX Report's p75 for the homepage, a service page and a blog post, on phone and desktop, with the whole-site (origin) figures as the fallback for a page with too little traffic. Low weight in the score (unscored where the full report's Lighthouse run already scores speed), and both reports name the source and the 28-day period.
**Impact priority** (`v5/code/_impact.js`): severity × the share of pages affected × the clicks and impressions those pages get in Search Console × their place in the site. ### The Phase 2 live check (P2-1 … P2-7, 2026-10-12)
Seven defects that passed the harness and failed live. The **menu** the describer reads comes from the site model's raw-HTML `nav_pages` (P2-1); the **services** the describer finds are written back into the model here (*Model Services Row*) and read by the Site Tracker from the stored description, so `services_json` is no longer `[]` (P2-2); every URL the **package** promises is on the canonical host and `url_lint.py` now watches Blog Package too (P2-3, stored rows: `fix_ladder_hosts.py`); the weekly report counts **days** again (P2-4); a `verdict` for a search one of the site's pages already answers **improves that URL** (P2-5); the **author box**'s bracketed fields are counted as `profile_placeholders` and keep the page from passing, without forcing an editor round (P2-6); and the **length** the ladder verdict set is stored on the row and clamps every later page run (P2-7).

### Minor items are folded, not hidden (G18-2, 2026-10-12)
The accuracy set measured **useful precision 75%**: 10 of the 40 findings shown on the three labelled sites were true and not worth a customer's time (the link count of a navigation page, a title one character over 60, "light content" on an index page, a URL rename that would cost rankings, a cosmetic tag).
`IMP.isMinor` (`v5/code/_impact.js`) marks the **minor band** — Low / Info, never an index blocker, the lowest impact or one of those measured rules — and every finding carries `minor`. Both audit reports list the main findings as before and fold the minor ones into one **"Minor items (N)"** line with the count and the reason; the Action Plan counts them instead of repeating them; `minor_count` travels in the callback and the app's technical page folds the same rows (`app/shared/src/findings.ts`, the same rule over the stored severity and impact).
Nothing is suppressed: the findings are scored, stored and listed inside the folded line.

### A reservation nobody settles, and one heavy crawl per site (P34-5, 2026-10-12)
Two 200-page audits of the same site started two seconds apart; the n8n **JavaScript task runner** stopped answering, both executions hung and were cancelled at the 90-minute timeout, and their `seo_run_ledger` rows stayed **reserved** — holding $0.77 of the $6/day estimate with nothing running.
**Released:** *Release Stale Runs* marks every reservation older than `CONFIG.run_stale_hours` (2) as `stale`, and **Rate Limit** leaves stale rows out of the day's count and of the budget whether that update got through or not. `release_stale_runs.py` clears the rows left from before this deploy (`--dry-run` by default).
**Refused:** the reservation now carries `domain` and `heavy` (mode `audit` from `CONFIG.heavy_audit_pages` pages up), and a second heavy audit of the same site is refused while the first one is still reserved, with the reason and how long to wait.

### What the keyword research is allowed to use (G8, criteria K2 / K4 / K6 / K7)
**Your own Search Console searches seed the research** (*Load Query History (Discovery)* → *Search Console Seeds (Discovery)*): the newest 28-day period, brand and SEO-tool queries dropped with the weekly report's own rules, keeping the searches **no page of yours answers** (page inventory, `SM.matchPage`) and the ones you rank **8-20** for. They go into the seed list behind the primary seed and ride on the pulls the research makes anyway — **no new call**.
**Traffic potential says what it is:** `calibrated` where Search Console measured that exact search on your site (impressions and clicks over 28 days, never below the clicks you already get), `modelled` from the provider's volume everywhere else, `unknown` when there is neither. Without Search Console data the number is unchanged.
**Clusters by shared results pages** (`KWI.serpClusters`): keywords that share **≥ 3** of the head keyword's top-10 URLs are one group named after that head keyword — one page can target them all.
**Live results-page checks**: `CONFIG.live_serp_checks` (**16**, hard cap 25, ~$0.002 each → ~$0.032 a run) instead of a fixed 8, with the per-topic cap growing with it.

### Original words, real images, a coverage target (G5 / G30 / G33, 2026-10-13)
**Originality (G5).** *Originality Check* sits between *Content QA* and *Needs Revision?* and measures the share of the draft's **8-word windows** that one single page also carries, against every competitor page this run read and the site's own pages it read. Over **`originality_max_overlap_pct` (15)** the quality check fails: the editor gets the passage quoted and the page named. The page being improved is exempt (a rewrite keeps its text); other inventory pages are reported as **duplicate targets** by title and slug.
**Images (G30).** *Image Cards* → *Render Images* (Gotenberg `/forms/chromium/screenshot/html`, local and free) → *Attach Images*: the hero and the two in-body figures are produced as **WebP** from the page's own content, under the planned file names, alt text and sizes, listed in `meta.json`, attached to the e-mail and sent in the callback. A card that cannot be rendered stays a plan with its reason.
**Coverage (G33).** The target is the **best** competitor's term coverage (clamped 60-90%), with its subtopics and depth: stated in the brief, scored in the quality check, reported with its basis.

### Google's own view of every key page, and a fix checked in days (G25 / G11, 2026-10-13)
**URL Inspection within the quota:** Google allows **2,000 inspections a day and 600 a minute per property**. The audit asks about up to **100** of its indexable pages (home page first, then click depth, then inbound links) and the weekly Site Tracker rotates through **every** key page, **oldest inspection first**, up to 150 a run — each answer stored on the page's row in `seo_page_watch`, which is what makes the rotation possible. Both reports print, per page: in Google's index or not, the state, **the canonical Google chose** against ours, the last crawl, **mobile usability** and the rich results. Whatever the budget did not reach, whatever failed and missing access are printed as **"not checked"** with the reason — never as "fine", never as "not indexed" (`v5/code/_page_watch.js`).
**Checked in days, not months:** the daily **SEO Agent — Page Watch** (05:45, free: one GET per key page + robots.txt) alerts on a page gone, a `noindex`, a moved canonical, a changed title or a changed robots.txt the same day, and re-checks any finding the owner marks as fixed on those pages within a day. Both audit reports say so where the fix list starts.

### Annotations, change tests and lineage (G12 + G29)
**Every chart is marked** with what happened: pages that went live (`seo_content_log.published_at`), technical audits with the findings they cleared (`seo_audits`), **Google updates** and **data breaks** (the num=100 break of September 2025) — from one dated file, `v5/data/seo_events.json`, inlined into `_annotations.js`, `_site_stats.js` and the app (`seo-events.generated.ts`). Add an update there and rebuild; a date with no event produces no mark.
**A page change is read like a won link**: `_change_test.js` (CT) compares the page's own move with the site's **other pages** over the same weeks (`seo_link_impact`, `kind: page_change`). Verdicts stay graded — *likely helped · possibly helped · no clear effect yet · too early to tell · can't tell* — and nothing ever says a change **caused** a move.
**Every figure carries its lineage** (`_lineage.js`): source, period, sample and how it was arrived at, as fields beside the value, one short note under the figures and a **"Where these numbers come from"** table in the weekly, AI-visibility, AI-growth, backlink, link-building, rank-tracker, ladder-plan and full reports. Modelled numbers say so; where the source was never recorded it reads **"source not recorded"**.

### What the re-rating run found (R1 … R9, 2026-10-13)
**R1 (High):** a page run the day's AI budget refused left its `seo_ladders` row at **writing**, and the ladder plan, the Rank Tracker and the Content Cadence then all reported a page that does not exist (exec 500 / row 19). **Refused Ladder Row → Release Ladder Row** puts the row back to `planned` with the reason, the plan promises nothing before the run is accepted, and all three features count a page as written only when `seo_content_log` says **written**. `fix_phantom_pages.py` repairs the rows left from before (dry run by default).
**R9:** every scheduled run now reserves and settles its own `seo_run_ledger` row (AI Visibility, AI Pulse, AI Growth, Backlink Monitor, Audit Scheduler, Link Builder, Rank Tracker, Site Tracker, Content Cadence), and every row carries a **DataForSEO estimate** beside the Claude one — both audits used to carry `est_usd: 0` while each crawl cost $0.09.
**R2** same category set on both sides of the audit diff · **R3** the topic fit retries in plain text and an unknown fit is in the label · **R4** a prospect on a competitor's or a SERP rival's registrable domain is refused (a "best X" list still passes) · **R5** a trigger-mode failure keeps its node, message and workflow · **R6** `seo_ops_alerts.delivered` records the channel that carried the alert · **R7** an FAQ section, never FAQPage schema · **R8** a rung page gets its length from the pages that rank for its ladder.

### Topic radius and the re-plan of a stuck ladder (G32) · the Link Builder's PDF (L3)
**Topic radius** (`_radius.js`, one kit for the research and the ladder): every topic is **within reach**, **a stretch** or **out of reach for now**, with the evidence printed next to the verdict — its difficulty against your measured reach, a position you already hold, a page you already have, a service you sell. A topic whose difficulty is inside the reach but which nothing you sell or write about names is a **stretch**, not a "now". It is shown with the plan and never enforced on it.
**A stuck ladder gets a proposal** (`_replan.js`, in the Rank Tracker): after the configured weeks without a position gain (`seo_monitors.stuck_weeks`, empty = 8) the weekly e-mail and the callback carry a re-plan — improve the page that already answers the search, write the easier supporting keyword, change the rung order, or stop — each with its reason and its evidence, and each marked **not applied**: a person accepts one in the app, nothing is rewritten for them.
**The Link Builder's week as a PDF** (L3): *LB Doc* + Gotenberg, attached to the e-mail and carried in the callback.

### The six defects the re-rating found (R10-R15, 2026-10-13)
**R10** Google retired the Mobile Usability report: `VERDICT_UNSPECIFIED`, a missing result or a FAIL with no issue list is **not checked** (`PW.inspection`), never "not mobile-friendly", and a finding with an empty evidence string is never raised. **Every** finding's clicks / impressions basis is now **capped at Search Console's own 28-day totals** (`IMP.rank`) - the live run claimed 720 clicks and 22,860 impressions for a site that measured 38 and 5,295.
**R11** A run that uses up `qa_max_rounds` with the gate still failing is delivered **as a draft**: the Word report, `meta.json`, the e-mail, the callback and the app all carry the **last** round's counts under "did not pass the quality check - not ready to publish". A passage the draft labels **illustrative** keeps its figures (the mask destroyed a worked example's arithmetic); unsourced real prices are still masked.
**R12** A Search Console row that names a page of this site is answered **by that page** - "the page that gets the impressions does not target this search" - never "no page of yours answers this search".
**R13** The fit gate measures **topic distance** (25%, the outreach bar) over every intent bucket and the gap; refusals are printed with their reasons and an emptied bucket says why.
**R14** The market-wide AI table identifies you by **domain**; a name-only row is dropped or labelled "not matched to your website" and never counted.
**R15** A ladder page keeps the **URL its ladder planned** (`ladder_target_url`) and lists every planned ladder link under `links_to_add_when_published`.

### What Claude costs, and where the estimates come from (G23, 2026-10-13)
**The three Opus nodes stream** (`streaming: true`, required above ~21k tokens), and a streaming call reports **no token usage at all** — so the page run's Claude cost could only ever be stated as a range, and `settled_usd` stored the *reservation* while every reader took it for a measured cost. Each call is now priced from what the run really knows: the characters its prompt interpolated, the characters it answered with and the thinking budget of its effort level (`v5/code/_cost_cal.js`, the call table baked from the real model nodes). It travels as `run_ledger.ai_cost` with **`estimated: true`** and a basis in words, and **Run Ledger Settle** writes `ai_usd`, `dfs_usd`, `measured_usd`, `estimated_usd` and `cost_basis` — measured and estimated money are never added up as one figure.
**The estimates now come from the money.** They were up to **13x** out (`ai_visibility` reserved $0.06 and cost $0.79; backlinks $0.04 for $0.37; the page $1.23 for $0.46), which is why the guard refused five runs that cost a fraction of the reservation. Both tables are recalibrated from the measured runs and **self-correcting**: **Cost Calibration Row → Save Cost Calibration** moves each mode's rolling figure in `seo_cache` (`cost:ai:<mode>` / `cost:dfs:<mode>`) toward what the run cost, and the guard reserves `max(rolling x 1.25, the recent maximum)` — it may fall as a mode gets cheaper, never below what the mode actually cost.
**Once a month** the owner downloads the Anthropic Console usage export (CSV or JSON) and runs `reconcile_claude_cost.py` (dry run by default): it compares the month's ledger rows with the export per model, prints the correction factor and, with `--apply`, writes it to `cost:factor:claude`, which every price then goes through.

### A stored rung nobody revisited, alerts on statistics, and a pre-release check (R16 · G28 · G27)
**R16 — the gate also reads what is already stored.** The keyword fit gate stopped new keywords; `seo_ladders` still held *"facts erp"* (a competitor's brand) as a planned rung, so the Rank Tracker reported it and the cadence would have written it. `fitStored` (in `_fit_gate.js`) now runs on the **read** path: the Content Cadence leaves such a rung out with its reason and marks the row **`set_aside`**, the Rank Tracker buys no check for it and names it instead of asking for the page. A rung whose page is already written is **kept and flagged**, never dropped. `fix_brand_rungs.py` repairs today's rows (dry run by default).
**G28 — the last fixed threshold is gone.** A keyword's position is an impression-weighted 28-day average: five places on 12 impressions is one search, not a drop. `ST.position` needs **50 impressions in both periods** before it calls a move real, tests the same keyword's clicks (Poisson z) and every alert now says **what was tested, over what period and how sure it is** (`ST.tested`), with Google's update dates as context.
**G27 — a pre-release check for CI.** `POST /webhook/seo-prerelease` runs the key-page checks (status, redirect, `noindex`, robots.txt, canonical, title, H1, description) against a **staging host or URL list** and answers `{ verdict, exit_code, failures, counts }`. It **writes nothing** (no Data Table node, no sub-workflow), and index coverage, real-user speed and positions come back as **`not_checked` with the reason** — a staging URL Google has never seen cannot be asked.
**Also:** a page type stored as free text is mapped to one of the form's options (the sentence kept as `page_notes`), and the fix pack no longer asks you to add a `sameAs` profile your homepage already lists.

### Nothing confident without the data under it (R23 · R22 · R26)
A ladder is a bet on the competition for one search. When the **live results page could not be read**, or the keyword research came back with fewer than 5 keywords around the head term, the plan is **refused**: no rungs, no score, no page run — the reason is in the plan, in its label and in the report ("Not scored — the data this rests on was missing"). Exec 549 planned, scored *winnable 68* and wrote a page from **one** keyword on a results page that had failed twice.
Every rung keyword is measured against the **head's own topic** (`_radius.js` `RAD.headFit`): half of the head's meaningful words have to be there. "azure api management monetization" is not a rung of "azure cloud migration dubai"; what is left out is listed with its reason.
A rung page's **length target is never 0** — the median of the pages read on the topic's results page, else the main page's target, else the competitor analysis, else a stated default — and the plan says which. The **Keyword Check** carries "no search data" in the label and gives no chance band when volume and difficulty are both unknown.

### What the second re-rating found (R21 / R20 / R25 / R27, R22's editor half — 2026-10-14)
**R21:** a prospect is a rival when its **registrable** domain matches a declared competitor or a domain the rank checks saw above us (`ae.invoiceq.com` → `invoiceq.com`), and a page that **sells what you sell** is refused on its own evidence, list or no list; "add us to your list" survives only on a page that really is a list.
**R20:** chart marks compare an audit only with the previous report **of the same kind** — a full report between two technical audits is marked as a different report, never as a score move.
**R25:** every bracketed figure left in the body is named to the owner, not only when there are more than five of them (the publish gate is unchanged).
**R22 (editor):** over length is an instruction — how many words to cut and from which sections — not one warning among twenty.
**R27:** a show's quote is prose from its **own description**, cut on word boundaries, and a guest appearance needs a 40% topic match.

### An answer that arrived with HTTP 200 and was still a failure (R18 / R19 / R24)
**One rule, one kit** (`v5/code/_dfs_retry.js`): DataForSEO answers a dead task with `status_code` 40101 inside an HTTP 200 and Google's URL Inspection with an `error` object — n8n's `retryOnFail` never sees either. Every gate (SERP, facts search, keyword data, URL inspection) now judges the answer with `RT`, **pauses and asks once more**, and never re-sends what a second attempt cannot fix (permission, property, quota).
**Where the retry fails too, nothing is scored on it.** The evidence is `unavailable`, the keyword verdict is **NOT CHECKED** with no score, no expected visits and no time to rank, and the first reason says why. A verdict computed on a results page nobody saw is worse than no verdict.
**Counts carry their sample.** Every indexing finding says how many pages Google actually answered for, the number is stored on the finding row, and the next audit **refuses to print a delta** when the two counts were measured on samples more than 20% apart — it says the sample moved.
**Schema, once:** a technical audit does not assess it (it has only the crawler's yes/no flag), so it emits no Schema finding and says so in "not assessed". The full SEO report assesses, weights and compares it.

### The money a run reports is the money that happened (R31 / R32 / R33, 2026-10-14)
**A crawl is billed for what it does.** DataForSEO quotes an on_page task when it is created — $0.0900 for the **200 pages asked for** — and repeats that quote in every later answer; audit 588 settled it as *measured* while **47** pages were crawled and the account fell **$0.0320** (+181%). The crawl is priced from the pages the crawl itself reported (`CC.crawlCost`), labelled **ESTIMATED**, with the quote, the request and the pages crawled in its basis. The rest of the DataForSEO figure is still what each task reported, so a settled row carries a measured half and an estimated half.
**A run that called no model settles nothing.** The `free_only` backlink check settled $0.05 of Claude with no model node in its trace while telling the caller $0. Every monitor settle now knows its own Claude nodes (written in at build time from the workflow) and a free site reserves nothing at all.
**Every branch prices its own calls.** G23's per-call pricing ran only inside the five report builders, so `describe` settled the $0.06 it reserved where its Haiku node reported 4,874 / 1,306 tokens ($0.0114). The same call table runs in **Run Ledger Settle**: a reservation is a guard, a settlement is a measurement.
**And the schedules joined the reconciliation:** every scheduled run takes the free `appendix/user_data` reading on its ledger chain, and **Page Watch** keeps a $0 row — free today, visible the day it is not.

### The guard watches all the money, and the account is the limit (2026-10-15, benchmark area 13)
**`ai_budget_usd` guarded a third of the bill.** DataForSEO was **$2.3876 of the $3.63** the 2026-10-14 re-rating cost, with nothing in
front of it. `dfs_budget_usd` is the same guard over the same period for the data money, with the same refusal: what the period used,
what this run would add, nothing charged, when it can run again.
**The account is a hard floor.** The free `appendix/user_data` reading R28 put on the ledger chain is read by the guard now: a run the
account cannot pay for — leaving `dfs_balance_floor_usd` for the scheduled checks — is refused **before** it spends, instead of running
out of credit half way and delivering half a report. A probe that did not answer reads 0 and refuses nothing.
**And a settled run stops counting its reservation:** the day's data total took `dfs_usd || dfs_est_usd`, so a free run that really spent
$0 held its $0.45 against the day for ever.
`run_cost_estimate_usd` carries the engine's own calibrated figure for the whole run, so what the caller is told and what the guard
reserves are one number.

You edit ONLY the sections listed under SECTIONS TO EDIT: every other part of the page is kept exactly as it is and is not shown to you. {{ ($('Verified Sources').first().json.page_contract || {}).text || '' }}

{{ ($('Verified Sources').first().json.style_guide || {}).prompt_block || '' }}

Primary keyword: {{ $('Verified Sources').first().json.keyword }} · Language: {{ $('Verified Sources').first().json.language_name || 'English' }} ({{ $('Verified Sources').first().json.spelling }} spelling) · Page type: {{ $('Verified Sources').first().json.page_type }}

'duration or timeline' : ''].filter(Boolean).join(', and no ') + ' and no bracket asking for one, and never add a promise (a deliverable, a pack, a guarantee) that the facts do not state. A subtopic of a competitor page that is a course, a fee or a product of another kind is not ours to cover.' : '' }}

FACTS ABOUT THE BUSINESS YOU MAY STATE (nothing else about it)
{{ [...((($('Verified Sources').first().json.content_brief || {}).client_facts) || []), $('Verified Sources').first().json.business_facts || '', $('Verified Sources').first().json.case_facts_text || ''].filter(Boolean).join(' | ') || 'none on file: write nothing about what the business does beyond its name and the services the page is about' }}

{{ [ ...((($('Verified Sources').first().json.content_brief || {}).evidence_plan) || []).map(e => '- ' + e.source_url + ' : ' + e.fact), ...((($('Verified Sources').first().json.page_fix || {}).sources) || []).map(v => '- ' + v.url + ' (fetched today' + (v.figure ? ', states ' + v.figure : '') + '): "' + String(v.evidence || '').slice(0, 260) + '"') ].join('\n') || 'none: a number that needs a source is taken out, or the sentence is rewritten without it' }}
Never write a URL that is not in this list or already in the section: a guessed address is removed automatically, and a claim that none of these sources backs is rewritten without the number or deleted.

ALLOWED INTERNAL LINKS (pages of this site that are live): {{ JSON.stringify((($('Verified Sources').first().json.content_brief || {}).internal_link_suggestions || []).map(l => l.url)) }}

HOW TO FIX THE USUAL PROBLEMS
- A statement about the business that nothing on file supports: rewrite it as advice to the reader ("a sound migration starts with ...") or as a neutral fact about the topic, or delete it. Never "we do", "our process", "you get from us" unless the facts above say it.
- A call to action: invite the reader to get in touch the way the facts say; never promise a deliverable, a timeline, a price or a result.
- A figure the source does not state, or a number with no source: quote the number the source above states, with its link, or rewrite the sentence so it does not need the number.
- "Cut about N words": take out repetition, restatements and secondary detail; keep every fact with its source, every link, the heading and any table.
- "Add about N words": add specific, useful detail (an example, a step, a decision rule, a trade-off) from the facts and sources above; never filler.

- A question heading: "### <the question>" with a 40-60 word direct answer right under it. Never a "Frequently Asked Questions" block or a Q1: / A1: list.

=== SECTION s3 ===
<the whole corrected section, starting with its heading line ("# ..." for s0, "## ..." for the others)>
=== END s3 ===
Write the closing line of every block. A section you could not improve is returned unchanged inside its block.

### The tokens Anthropic counts, and the run the account can answer for (B-A8 / B-A5, 2026-10-15)
**Nothing in this engine measured a Claude token.** Checked against the running instance, not assumed: `@langchain/anthropic`'s
streaming `_generate` returns no `llmOutput`, so n8n records a tiktoken `tokenUsageEstimate` for the three Opus nodes — and the real
`tokenUsage` of the other eight rides the `ai_languageModel` connection, which `WorkflowDataProxy` never reads. A Code node cannot see
one token of it.
**So the measurement arrives on the main path.** Anthropic's **free** `count_tokens` endpoint counts the exact prompt each streaming
agent rendered and that prompt plus the exact answer — two free calls per agent, `neverError`, falling back to characters if either is
silent. The difference is the answer's own tokens. Only the **thinking** no counter can see stays modelled, from the effort budget, and
it is the only estimate left in those calls: `CC.callCost` now splits every call into measured and estimated money instead of throwing
the whole call into one bucket.
**And the run, not only the day, is held against the account.** A second free `appendix/user_data` reading on the settle chain, the
ledger rows reloaded around this run's window, and the move attributed to the run **only when no other row was open across it** —
otherwise the run keeps its per-task figure and says why. `settled_at`, `dfs_balance_end` and `dfs_source` say which figure the row
carries.

### The run cost the engine worked out and told nobody (2026-10-15, B-R3)
`run_cost_estimate_usd` — Claude plus DataForSEO, from the same self-correcting estimates the guard reserves against — existed in
**two** places in every generated workflow: *Rate Limit*, and a sticky note about *Rate Limit*. No callback carried it, so no caller
and no customer ever saw it, while the app had already been built to prefer the engine's figure over its own.
It is now worked out **above** the four refusals (a refused run carried none, because every `return` happened first), and stamped on
to every callback by **Run Cost (Callback)**, the one node between *Has Callback?* and *POST Callback* that all eleven response
builders funnel through. The build walks `main` from both triggers and fails if a builder or *POST Callback* can be reached without
passing *Rate Limit*, so the twelfth builder cannot quietly ship without it.
**It says what it is** (INVARIANTS rule 1): `run_cost_estimate_state: 'modelled'`, with the basis naming what it was modelled from —
or `'not_available'` with the reason and a **null** amount, never a 0. What the run really spent stays `run_ledger`, settled at the end.
**Not on the 202:** *Rate Limit* runs after the front door has answered, and a second estimator there is the very bug B-R3 exists to
kill.

### An alert nobody received, and nine schedules that could not be refused (B-A7 / B-A9, 2026-10-15)
**Every alert is re-attempted until something receives it, or until the row says it gave up.** `seo_ops_alerts` carries `attempts`, `last_attempt_at`, `next_attempt_at` and one line per attempt in `attempt_log`. The retry has no schedule of its own: the last thing every scheduled run does — and every run of the Error Handler — is sweep up to 5 alerts that have reached nobody and re-send them (30 minutes between tries, `critical` from the 3rd, given up after 10 and never called delivered). A row is marked delivered **only on a 2xx**: `Post Alert Webhook` is `neverError`, so without `fullResponse` a 404 from a revoked hook read as a success.
**The ten schedules pass the same concurrency gate as the API runs** (`v5/code/_run_guard.js`, shared with *Rate Limit*): the same monitor already in flight, a heavy crawl of the same site, more than 3 analyses at once, or an account that cannot pay for the run. A refused schedule marks its ledger row `refused` before the first paid node and ends there; it is never refused on the Claude or DataForSEO budget.

### One cause, not five symptoms — and the links nothing can follow (B5-1 / B5-2 / B5-3)
**The crawl reads the first response** (JavaScript off by default), so an H1 a script writes was reported as *"Missing H1 heading — add one clear H1 per page"* on a page whose H1 exists. Sitebulb's 2024 corpus puts that at **18.3% of pages**.
**Now:** where the response-versus-render check proved the figure is written by JavaScript on **half or more** of the key pages it read twice, the crawl-wide symptom is **joined to the cause** — one finding, the higher severity, the crawl's own count, the rendering fix, both titles kept in `merged_titles`, and **one deduction instead of two**.
**And the audit says what it read**: "Every page figure in this report was read from the first response."
**Links nothing can follow** (Screaming Frog v24 parity, free): `<a>` with no href or a `javascript:` href that navigates on click, and div / span / li / button / tr carrying an address in `onclick` or `data-href` — read from HTML already fetched, and named as the usual cause of the orphan pages the crawl reports.

### A plan measured on its own topic, and an order that says why (B2-1 · B2-2 · B2-3, 2026-10-15)
**Reach was one number for the whole website**, cached 30 days — so the same 10 measured on e-invoicing research decided the plan for "erp implementation dubai" (`lad_mv5pjt5y4aoa`, 2026-10-13). The ladder now measures the reach **on its own topic** from the keywords the site already ranks for, with the same on-topic test the rungs use, and uses it only when at least 5 on-topic top-10 keywords stand behind it. Otherwise the site-wide reach stays and the plan says so: *"treat the months and the chance below as the optimistic case."* Absence of on-topic wins never invents a penalty.
**The plan opens with what you already have on the topic** — pages, searches you rank for, your best position — and states its own improve-vs-new split. A search an existing page already answers never gets a second page.
**Every planned page carries the figures that put it there**: its difficulty against the reach actually used, its keywords and volume, its intent, whether it is new or an improvement, and that it links up to the main page.

### The number a source states, and a gate that has to refuse (B3-1 · B3-2 · B3-3, 2026-10-15)
**The money mask knew less than the figure check beside it.** It ran first and rewrote the draft for good, judging an amount only against the facts on file — while the check forty lines later kept any other figure a cited source stated. So one sentence of one fetched page kept its "42%" and lost "AED 5,000", "AED 500" and "AED 10,000". The delivered penalties page shows it: **43 × [Price]**, its own Fine column included, under a correct citation of the decision that states every fine — and those 43 tokens are what put the page over the placeholder limit and had it refused. Both checks now read **one** corpus, and an amount a source cited **in that sentence** states is kept, with the source named.
**A fine is never our price.** "costs" is a price word, so "the penalty costs AED 5,000 per month" was erased instead of being put in front of the reviewer. A fine, penalty, threshold, levy, duty or violation now always keeps its number as `[Confirm: …]`.
**And what the mask does remove is named**, with the sentence it came from: `[Price] x43` is nothing an owner can answer.
**A gate that fails must refuse, not label.** *Originality Check* runs after *Content QA* has already finalised the delivery gate, and flipped only `passed`. On the last round a draft **100% identical to a competitor page** came out `publishable: true`, `not_ready: false`, *"passed the quality check"* — which is what the file name, the package banner, meta.json, the callback and the app all read. It now re-decides the gate it invalidated.

### A page losing traffic is tested, then refreshed (B4-1 · B4-2 · B4-3, 2026-10-15)
**The old rule called any 25% fall on 10 earlier clicks a "decaying page"** — the one window that cannot tell a decay from a seasonal dip, at a volume this system's own test rejects (10 → 7 clicks is z = −0.73). A page is now decaying only when the fall survives the **two-sample Poisson test** *and* is not the dip the same weeks had **a year ago** (one more free Search Console request). Clicks down while impressions held is named a **click-through** loss — title and description first, not a rewrite.
**What is refused is still reported**: seasonal, watch and too-small each say so, with the clicks they were measured on.
**And then it becomes work.** The judgement is stored on the page's `seo_pages` row, and the Content Cadence writes the **refresh** of that URL — ranked by the clicks actually lost, ahead of striking distance and rising trends, at most 2 a week, never within 60 days of the last refresh. Ladder rungs still come first.

### One search, one page — decided by the results page, not by a label (B2-4 · B2-5, 2026-10-15)
**The rungs were grouped by the AI's topic label**, because the ladder's four Labs pulls return no URLs and `Ladder Pool` left `competitors` empty — so two searches Google answers with **the same pages** could become two pages, the duplication this system forbids everywhere else.
**Now the ladder buys one results page per rung candidate** (capped at 24 = **$0.048**, free runs buy none) and groups them the way Keyword Insights does: **the top 7 at 40% shared URLs**. A cluster takes its head keyword's rung, so the difficulty bands cannot undo it, and a group built on evidence is never split in two.
**A keyword whose results page failed twice is named, not clustered and not dropped** — the plan prints how many could not be compared, with the provider's own reason, and what the comparison really cost (counted once per task id).
**And the destination's results page is counted**: distinct **registrable** domains in the top 10 (Semrush's fifth factor). Five or fewer own it → the feasibility score is 6 lower; six or seven → 3. The count is measured, the adjustment is a stated rule, and the report prints both.

### A number we report is measured, or it says what it is (INVARIANTS rule 1)
`lineage_lint.py` walks the **generated** workflows at build time and fails the build on four things, so none of them can be reintroduced: a node that composes a document a customer receives without carrying `_lineage.js`; a **finding with an empty evidence string**; a **delta** computed across a different `report_type` or a sample that moved; a **score** with no way of being withheld when its inputs are unavailable.
**Paid here:** the audit's seven site-wide findings (SSL, HTTPS redirect, sitemap, robots.txt, 404, directory browsing, HTTP/2) stated **nothing** a reader could check - they now name the check that produced them; `LN.evidenced` runs at the sink (*Build Site Issues*, after every module's findings are merged, before scoring) and the report's notes say what it held back; and the **technical site audit** gained the "Where these numbers come from" table the full report has had since G29.
**Ratcheted, not proven:** `harness/lineage_baseline.json` names today's unpaid debt. The lint proves no NEW node can join a class; it does not prove that every figure inside a passing node carries its own lineage.

### Nothing is promised until it exists, and nothing exists until it is delivered (INVARIANTS rule 4)
`state_lint.py` walks the **generated** workflows at build time and fails the build on six things: a node that mints `written` / `published` into a stored row without reading the evidence; a call of the shared published-row builder that does not **hand it the proof**; a **Data Table node** that mints a forward state with no gate in front of it; a `writing` state with no way back; a **delivery written down without a status code** (or read from an HTTP node that is `neverError` with no `fullResponse` — how a 404 from a revoked webhook was recorded as a delivery); and a later gate that refuses on one field while the fields the file name, the banner, meta.json, the callback and the app read still say the page passed.
**Found and paid here:** "I published a page" wrote `status: 'published'`, the URL and `page_exists: true` for a page that had just answered **404** — while telling the owner, in the same run, that it could not be fetched; and *Mark Case Study Published* marked the case study live with no gate at all. Both now need the proof.
**Ratcheted, not proven:** `harness/rule4_baseline.json` (empty today). The lint does not prove the row a passing node wrote is the row its evidence covers, and the app-side half of B-R1 is enforced in `app/`.

### The five defects rule 1's lint found (B-L1 … B-L5)
**Two wrong numbers reaching a customer.** *AI Metrics* subtracted the last run's **share of voice** and **visibility score** without checking the question panel was the same size — the panel is settable from **3 to 50**, so growing it read as a collapse (B-L4, R19's shape). *Parse Backlinks* alerted on a 15-point **spam score** move without checking the two snapshots were built from the same sources — a `free_only` check buys nothing from DataForSEO (B-L5, R20's shape). One guard for both: `RT.likeForLike` + `RT.comparable`, and the reason is printed where the arrow would have been.
**Three figures with no provenance.** The written-page package (B-L1) printed the content score, topic coverage and originality whether or not the check behind them had anything to work with — a score whose check did not run is now **withheld, with the reason**. The keyword strategy (B-L2) printed provider **estimates** for a single keyword as facts and shipped with no lineage table at all. The **Word attachment** (B-L3) dropped the lineage block, so the customer who opened the file saw every number without its source — every report type renders through that one node.

### An answer nobody asked twice for (B-A10, 2026-10-15)
**DataForSEO reports most failures inside an HTTP 200**, which `retryOnFail` never sees. R18 gated three paths by hand; **49 calls across 12 workflows** were still outside a gate — the shape that planned, scored and wrote a whole ladder on two results pages that had both failed (exec 549).
**One splice, not twenty hand-wired chains** (`dfs_gate.py`): plan → wait → one more attempt → merge. Only a failure a second attempt can help is re-sent, and **nothing at all** when the requests and the answers cannot be paired one to one.
**A retry cannot double-charge.** A failed task is billed 0; where both attempts were billed, the cost sums both and counts each task **once by its own id**, and every retry node is on the ledger's list. *Start Crawl* never re-sends an empty result — that would be a second crawl.
**What stays, and why.** The twelve free `appendix/user_data` balance probes (they fail open and nothing scores on them) and *Get Crawl Summary* (it is already a poll loop). Each keeps its reason in `harness/in200_baseline.json`.

### The other half of every Claude figure, and three nodes that advised from what they could not read (B-F1 / B-A11, 2026-10-15)
**B-F1.** Section 62 counted the three streaming Opus agents and left the eight non-streaming ones on characters. They are counted here by the same two **free** `count_tokens` calls on the **main** path. Three things the code had to settle: the prompt is re-read against the agent's input node **with its output index spelled out** (*Keyword Seeds* hangs off output **1** of *Route Mode*, and `.first()` defaults to the output the ACTIVE node is connected to); *Keyword Relevance* and *Ladder Keyword Relevance* answer **once per chunk**, so their counts are summed and `rounds` says how many calls the sum covers; and **the Critic is not a loop** — walking `main` shows no path back to it, so `qa_round` had been multiplying a call that happened once.
**Still modelled, and always will be:** the thinking a model does before answering is billed as output and never returned. *Site Describer* has no thinking budget, so it is the one node that is 100% measured.
**Not counted, and recorded (`harness/claude_count.json`):** the **eleven** Claude agents in the other seven workflows, which are not character-priced at all — a monitor settles its RESERVATION. `_b76_checks` fails the build on a new uncounted agent.
**B-A11.** *Pick Competitors*, *Competitor Analysis* and *Analyze Keywords* each turned a read that had failed **twice** into a measured-looking zero — a **High** "does not rank in the top 10 for any keyword" among them. Each now carries the gate's `__dfs`, hands on `null`, and says "could not be read". The class is now **check E of `lineage_lint.py`**, with 19 consumers on the ratchet.

### The verdict’s own two numbers, and a difficulty measured on the topic (B1-1 · B1-2 · B1-3, 2026-10-15)
**“Time to rank: 6 months” and “Expected visits/month at #1-3: 70” came out of the language model** and reached the Word file, the PDF and the ladder card with no basis at all. They are now **computed**: the plan’s month range with its uncalibrated chance band, and the volume through the **measured** click loss of the results page that was read — each printed with what it is. A results page nobody could read produces no visit figure at all.
**Difficulty is measured on the topic**, as MarketMuse and Semrush do it: the reach cache keeps the keywords it was measured on, so the Keyword Check, the keyword report and discovery can measure the difficulty this site has already beaten **on this topic**. Below five on-topic top-10 keywords the site-wide number stays — never a penalty — and the answer says which number it used and on what.
**The AI Overview click loss was the April 2025 figure (0.65).** December 2025: −58.0% at position 1, −50.8% at 2, −46.4% at 3 (Ahrefs, 300,000 keywords). Every traffic potential on an AI Overview page was ~1.5x too generous.

### The pages the crawl never reached, and a queue that starts with what changed (B5-5 / B5-8)
**B5-5.** G24 told the truth — "Crawled 47 of 112 known URLs" — and then judged the site on the 47. The other 65 were a **number**: never opened, although a URL the crawler could not reach is exactly the kind that 404s, redirects or carries a `noindex`.
*Not Crawled Targets → Fetch Not Crawled → Not Crawled Check* now reads up to **25** of them with one **free plain GET** each (redirects not followed, so a redirect is the answer) and reports gone / redirecting / noindex / canonicalised elsewhere / **live and indexable and never audited**. **$0.**
**A page we could not fetch is reported as not fetched, with the reason** — a timeout, a DNS failure or a bot wall is `not_checked`, never a finding; every count carries `checked` / `checked_of`; with nothing readable the block is "not assessed" with its reason.
**B5-8.** Ahrefs' Always-On Audit picks its next URL partly from **IndexNow** pings. We operate IndexNow for the customer and write their pages, and used neither: both queues were "oldest reading first". `PW.changedPages` reads `seo_ai_pages.submitted_at`, `seo_content_log.published_at` and `seo_ai_targets.written_at` (**read-only**) and `PW.freshFirst` puts what changed in the last **7 days** in front of Google's URL-Inspection rotation and of the not-crawled queue. A table that could **not be read** says so — which is not the same answer as "nothing changed this week".

### One AI Overview figure in one place, and a state that advances only on evidence (B6-9 / B9-6)
**B6-9 (INVARIANTS rule 1).** *Ladder Pool* kept its own copy of the SERP click-loss table, with the **April 2025** AI Overview figure (a flat 35% loss) that B1-3 had removed from the discovery kit and B6-1 from the rank kit. A flat factor cancels out of a *share* — which is why the share of voice needed a per-position table — but this is an absolute estimate, and only the keywords whose results page has an AI Overview carried it, so it inflated those estimates by 1.35x **and moved them up the order that decides which rungs are planned**. The ladder now makes the same `KWI.calibrate` call discovery makes, and the number carries its basis. A **build-time scan** refuses `0.65` beside an AI Overview in any kit or node, with comments stripped first, so the fourth copy fails the build.
**B9-6 (INVARIANTS rule 4).** An AI target was marked `writing` when a page run *started*, and **nothing ever set `written`** — a refused or failed run left the question claiming work in progress for ever, R1's class in the one table R1 did not cover. *AI Target Marks* now puts the row back to `queued` with the error when the spawn fails; **AI Target Settle** is the only exit, and it advances a row only against the `seo_content_log` row for that same run (R1's rule: a page counts as written only on a `written` content-log row). The 14-day requeue stays in AI Growth, so there is one rule in one place.
**And the class:** `state_lint.py`'s "a work-in-progress state needs a way back" was asked only of the tables someone had listed — which is how `seo_ai_targets` sat outside it for three releases. The list is now **derived from the generated workflows**, and a table whose `writing` state is read back and acted on fails the build until its way back is declared *and* built. It found a third table on its first run, `seo_case_studies`, and records the honest answer: nothing tests that row's state, so it is not this defect.

### The verdict reads the whole page before it says what the page lacks (R38, R52)
**R38 (High).** The report told a customer that their article had *no mandate dates, no tables, no author or date* — it has all three. Three cuts hid them (9,000, 3,500 and 5,000 characters), and the text reader flattens tables and drops bylines whatever the cut. The run now reads the page's own HTML for free (*Read Client Page HTML*), **measures the page's facts on the whole page** (*Collect Client Pages*: dates in the text, tables, byline, publication date, call to action; "NOT CHECKED" when the HTML was only a script shell), the analyzer / verdict / copywriter read those facts, **Check Page Claims** removes any analyzer gap the facts contradict, and *Parse Verdict* does the same to the verdict's own sentences (`v5/code/_page_claims.js`). A claim the page could not be checked for is not made.
**R52.** *Site Pages* named every menu page by the reader's title; on a client-rendered site that is one generic title. A title the homepage carries, or two pages share, is replaced by the menu link text.

### A run that knows who started it, a refusal that reaches the customer, an alert row that is updated (R77 / R81 / R116 / R96 / R79 / R105 / R95)
**R77.** An on-demand AI visibility or backlinks check is started by this workflow (*Monitor Start*), whose own ledger row has the same mode. The monitor now receives `parent_run_id` (this execution's id), names it in its ledger row (`parent:<id>`) and does not count that run as "another run in flight"; a genuine second run is still refused. **R81.** This run's row then settles **$0, handed off** — the money is on the monitor's row, counted once.
**R116 / R96.** A refused monitor ends at its own notice: an on-demand caller receives `{stage: rejected, status: rejected, error, request_id}` instead of waiting three hours; no balance read, no settle (the refusal settles its row itself).
**R79 / R105.** The ops-alert key is trimmed once when it is built; every write-back uses the key the row is stored with, byte for byte; *Alert Delivery* has one input (a merge of both channels), so the retry sweep runs once per failure; a re-sent row records the webhook in `channels`.

### A draft that failed its quality check is not a page to publish (R111, 2026-10-16)
*Content Log Row* stores `not_ready` + the last round's reasons (`qa_reasons`) when the page's **final** quality verdict failed; `written` keeps meaning "passed QA, waiting to be published". Every reader says **"fix the draft and run it again"** instead of "publish it": the weekly site report (`fix_draft`), the Rank Tracker, the cadence's pile-up note ("needs a fix", still counted), the site brief, the AI targets. Publish detection still finds one the owner publishes anyway. Rows written before this deploy: `fix_not_ready_drafts.py` (dry run by default).

### One picture of the results page and of our own pages (R87 R88 R90 R91 R93 R92 R59, 2026-10-16)
**R87:** one results page is read **one entry per position** (the report counted every page-1 domain twice and set "e invoicing in uae" aside as government on two government sites of five); a head that IS set aside **pauses its ladder** — report, ladder row (*Tracker Ladder Marks*), plan, cadence, app. **R90:** a stored rung is judged against its ladder's stored results pages and the AI brand names ("facts erp" / facts.ae). **R88:** one baseline per keyword per run, and a change no larger than two readings of one moment is "noise". **R91:** "top 50". **R93:** our pages by their real titles. **R92 / R59:** "countries", a covered ladder target reported as the live page, the bare-host / www split Google chose named with its fix.

## A refresh re-checks its facts (B3-8, 2026-10-16)
A page rewritten on top of its live version (the cadence's **decay** refresh, an AI refresh, any `existing_page_url` run) used to keep every figure it carried with its old citation unchecked: the figure check looks a number up only in a source the run read, and nobody read the live page's own sources.
*Refresh Source Plan* picks the live page's external links that sit **next to a figure** (max 8), *Fetch Refresh Sources* re-reads them with Jina, *Refresh Sources* passes them on. **Content QA** checks the draft against them (a missing figure becomes `[Confirm: …]`) and the **live page itself** (`content_qa.refresh_check`, report only). Not a refresh: nothing is fetched.

### The page and its gate (F-A2, re-rating 2026-10-17)
**Placeholders (A-13).** One detector (`v5/code/_placeholders.js`): a review note is one of `[Confirm: …]`, `[Owner: …]`, `[Author insight: …]`, `[Image: …]`; every other bracket that starts with a letter is a placeholder. The app reads the same two patterns.
**Links (A-14).** *Outbound Link Requests* → *Any Outbound Links?* → *Fetch Outbound Links* → *Outbound Link Check* fetch every outbound link on every QA round: 404 / 410 / no such domain / a "not found" page is **dead** and fails the gate (named by URL, with a replacement from this run's sources or "remove it"); a bot check, block or server error is "could not be checked".
**Claims (A-15 / A-19).** Statements about the business's own terms, scope and credentials are held against its facts, profile, site model and its own pages read in this run; unsupported ones are marked `[Confirm: …]`. Its own figures need no external source.
**Subtopics (A-16)** never name a company. **Protected blocks (A-17):** the Quick answer and source links survive the editor. **Exclusions (A-18):** the verdict's `topics_to_skip` reach the brief, the writer and the gate.

### The head keyword's results page: three attempts, the last one lighter (F-SERP, 2026-10-20)
DataForSEO's scraper answers **40101 "Internal SE Server Error."** inside an HTTP 200 for heavy requests at random (rehearsal execs 23 / 31: the client's own keyword came back NOT_CHECKED twice in a row). This read is the one a ladder cannot do without, so it is sent **up to three times**: wait 20 s, again; wait 45 s, then a **lighter** request (top 10, no AI Overview). Only what a further attempt can fix is re-sent; every attempt's cost is counted once by task id.
An answer from the lighter attempt says so: the AI Overview is **"not read on this attempt"**, never "none", and results below position 10 were not read. When all three fail the client reads, in plain words, that Google's results could not be read right now, that it is not about their keyword, and to try again later.

### The page pipeline (H1, 2026-10-27)
**Page Fix** (before every check): keyword in title / H1 / introduction, meta lengths, slug, Quick answer up, snippet headings, internal links, brand form, **no brackets** (the sentence goes, the question is kept for the client).
**Page Candidates** (after every check): dead links fixed, ONE score for every draft (hard blockers > soft blockers > advisory), **the best draft is kept**; then a **section-targeted edit** (at most 3, stop when nothing improves) or the **final version** (the system's own neutral rewrite) checked once more; then **ready / ready_with_questions / not_ready**, the grade of the delivered page, the client questions.
**Sources**: Page Source Plan -> SearXNG -> Fetch Page Sources -> **Verified Sources** (answers + states the figure); the Editor cites only those.
